title: Getting Started
intro: How to install ngspice, run it, write a netlist, and control how it starts up and which other simulators' syntax it accepts.

items: Installing and Running ngspice: packages and builds for Linux, Windows and macOS, batch, interactive and server modes, the command-line options, and where the output goes.
Netlist Syntax: the rules of a netlist file: title line, element lines, node names, numbers and scale factors, comments, continuation lines and dot commands.
Start-Up Files and Compatibility: spinit and .spiceinit, environment variables, compatibility modes for PSpice, LTspice, HSPICE, Spectre and KiCad netlists, and the settings PDK users need.

blocks.text: If you have never used SPICE, read them in order and run the samples as you go. If you have used another SPICE, skim Netlist Syntax and read Start-Up Files and Compatibility closely: most surprises when moving to ngspice come from there.
